<h1>Ran Wang</h1>
<p class="hero-name-alt">王冉</p>
<p class="hero-affiliation">School of Geographic Sciences, East China Normal University · M.Sc. in Human Geography, 2026</p>

<p class="hero-interests">Scientific mobility · Collaboration networks · Destination choice · Firm innovation measurement · Regional innovation</p>

My research examines how innovation is organized across space through the movement of highly skilled people, the formation of collaboration networks, and the innovation strategies of firms. I work with longitudinal career records, relational data, city-level indicators, and firm-year innovation data to study how individual decisions and institutional contexts shape regional innovation systems.

## Research Interests

::: {.interest-grid}
::: {.focus-item}
### Scientific Mobility and Career Trajectories

Intercity and inter-organizational mobility among elite biomedical scientists, with attention to career histories, institutional affiliations, and the spatial ordering of academic careers.
:::

::: {.focus-item}
### Collaboration Networks and Destination Choice

Coauthor ties, mobility ego-networks, pre-move relationships, and event-level destination choice among candidate cities.
:::

::: {.focus-item}
### Regional Innovation and City Networks

Urban scientific capacity, mobility-network structure, proximity, and the role of cities as organizational sites of knowledge production.
:::

::: {.focus-item}
### Firm Innovation Measurement

Firm-level innovation indicators built from R&D investment, patents, trademarks, industry, country, identity matching, and year-level panel construction.
:::
:::

:::

::: {.page-band}

## Academic Profile

::: {.profile-grid}
::: {.profile-item}
### Research Positioning

Economic geography and regional innovation, with a focus on how mobility, collaboration, and firm innovation data can be used to explain uneven innovation geographies.
:::

::: {.profile-item}
### Current Outputs

An accepted article in *World Regional Studies*, submitted manuscripts on elite biomedical scientist mobility, and ongoing work on destination choice and firm innovation measurement.
:::

::: {.profile-item}
### Data and Methods

Longitudinal data construction, scientist-institution-city linkage, social network analysis, conditional logit, GIS, remote-sensing indicators, and reproducible Python/R workflows.
:::
:::
